title: Personal Credit Cards: Cash Advance Charges, Cash Advance Ceiling and Foreign Transaction Fee
content:
Personal Credit Cards set three transaction-level figures per tier for cash drawn on the card and for purchases made abroad or in another currency: the cash advance fee (a percentage with a smallest amount), the share of the credit limit that cash advances in one statement cycle may reach, and the foreign transaction fee on qualifying purchases.

| Tier | Cash advance fee, percent of each advance | Smallest cash advance fee | Cash advances in one statement cycle, ceiling as a percent of the credit limit | Foreign transaction fee, percent of the purchase |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Secured Visa | 5.00 percent | 10.00 USD | 20 percent | 3.00 percent |
| College Rewards Visa | 5.00 percent | 10.00 USD | 20 percent | 3.00 percent |
| Platinum Low Rate Visa | 5.00 percent | 10.00 USD | 30 percent | 3.00 percent |
| Cash Rewards Visa | 5.00 percent | 10.00 USD | 30 percent | 3.00 percent |
| Travel Rewards Visa Signature | 5.00 percent | 10.00 USD | 30 percent | 0.00 percent |
| Visa Infinite Private Client | 5.00 percent | 10.00 USD | 40 percent | 0.00 percent |

## Q&A on these figures

- **What does a foreign transaction fee of 0.00 percent mean in practice?** On Travel Rewards Visa Signature and Visa Infinite Private Client a purchase transacted abroad, or priced in a currency other than US dollars, attracts no fee at all.
- **Is the cash advance ceiling a lifetime figure?** No; it bounds the total of cash advances posted within a single statement cycle.

> Hypothetical illustration: on a Cash Rewards Visa account with a 4000.00 USD limit, cash advances within one cycle may total no more than 30 percent of 4000.00 USD, which is 1200.00 USD. A 150.00 USD advance on any tier gives 5.00 percent of 150.00 USD, or 7.50 USD, which is below the 10.00 USD smallest fee, so 10.00 USD is billed.
